credit_stance.label: Credit Stance
credit_stance.explanation: Net of four risk votes (valuation, loss cycle, volatility, funding). Risk-off if net ≥ +2, risk-on if ≤ −2, else neutral.

credit_regime.label: Credit Regime
credit_regime.explanation: Driven by the Excess Bond Premium — the corporate-spread component beyond compensation for expected default. Low EBP = risk-on.

valuation.label: Valuation (cheap / rich)
valuation.explanation: OAS vs a macro fair value regressed on the 10y rate, 2s10s slope and VIX. Gap > 0 ⇒ spreads wide of fundamentals ⇒ cheap; < 0 ⇒ rich.

loss_cycle.label: Loss Cycle
loss_cycle.explanation: Logit-hazard forecast of the loss/charge-off rate from lagged credit and macro drivers; direction is the 4-quarter change.

volatility.label: Volatility
volatility.explanation: GARCH(1,1) conditional volatility of daily 10y-yield changes (a free MOVE proxy); elevated/low compares current vol to its long-run level.

funding.label: Funding Stress
funding.explanation: Money-market spreads (CP–bill, SOFR–IORB) z-scored into a composite stress regime — the plumbing that forces credit selling when tight.

policy_path.label: Policy Path
policy_path.explanation: Fed funds path from 3-month Treasury forwards, anchored to the current funds rate and corrected for forwards' historical over-prediction (median error −0.2 to −0.5pp). Band = 16-84% of the method's own past errors. Backtest 2000-25: RMSE 0.40 / 0.72 / 1.36pp at 3/6/12m vs no-change 0.46 / 0.84 / 1.52. The Taylor rule (core PCE, unemployment gap, estimated smoothing) loses to no-change as a forecast, so it is shown only as a gauge of how easy or tight policy is.

stress_lab.label: Stress Lab
stress_lab.explanation: Your macro shock runs through an assumed Fed reaction (1.5× core inflation, 0.8 / 0.4 pass-through to 2y / 10y, +0.3pp unemployment per +100bp), then through regressions of 4-quarter changes in spreads and losses on changes in VIX, unemployment, curve slope and bank tightening (1990+). HY / IG move 4× / 1× the Baa spread. Market variables phase in over the chosen months; losses move linearly to their 12-month change. These are average historical sensitivities, not a forecast of any one episode.

paper.cite: Hirtle, Kovner, Vickery & Bhanot (2016, JBF) — CLASS model

spread_outlook.label: Spread Outlook
spread_outlook.explanation: Median path and fan come from 40 years of Baa−10y spread history: h-month proportional moves, with history that started from a similar spread level given half the weight, scaled to each index. Backtest (310 monthly origins, 2000-25): spread levels are not forecastable beyond no-change (the median ties it and beats mean reversion), but the fan is calibrated — 5-95% band covered 87-91% — and beats a plain historical-moves distribution by 5-9%. Fair value is a cheap/rich signal (log VIX, slope, 10y), not a path driver.

soft_data.label: Beige Book Credit Stress
soft_data.explanation: Dictionary scoring of each Beige Book full report: credit-deterioration terms (delinquencies, charge-offs, tightening standards, weak loan demand, layoffs) minus easing terms, per 10k words, z-scored since 2001. Its 4q change leads charge-offs (corr +0.35) and feeds default_cycle_soft with SLOOS tightening; the level is coincident (recession AUC 0.90). Misfired in 2020 (stress without losses under fiscal support).

paper.cite: Balke & Petersen (2002, JMCB); Loughran & McDonald (2011, JF)

filings_distress.label: Filings Distress (EDGAR)
filings_distress.explanation: Share of SEC filings using distress language: 'going concern' in 10-K/10-Qs; 'forbearance agreement', 'restructuring support agreement' and Chapter 11 'voluntary petition' in 8-Ks. Log-shares z-scored since 2001. Validation: going-concern 4q change leads charge-offs (corr +0.50) and feeds default_cycle_filings; forbearance has recession AUC 0.74; RSA / Chapter-11 shares and the composite showed no signal.

floating_rate.label: Floating-Rate Coverage
floating_rate.explanation: Forward 1M Term SOFR (Pensford) + loan spread = direct-lending coupon; a lognormal leverage cross-section maps it to the share of borrowers whose EBITDA can't cover cash interest (ICR < 1x), baseline and stress.

Institutions noted past due loan levels are slightly elevated from historically low levels, and delinquency rates have remained steady.
Changes in loan demand ranged from slight decreases to moderate increases, and multiple contacts said higher borrowing rates dampened demand.
